passage_text: Researchers studied the effect of a novel dietary supplement on exercise performance in healthy adults. A randomized, double‑blind, placebo‑controlled trial enrolled 120 participants aged 18‑35 years. Participants were randomly assigned to receive either the supplement (n=60) or a matched placebo (n=60) for 8 weeks. Baseline measurements included body mass index (BMI), resting heart rate, and VO2max. After the intervention, participants performed a graded treadmill test to exhaustion, and time to exhaustion (TTE) was recorded. The supplement group exhibited a mean TTE increase of 12.5% (95% CI 8.3–16.7%) compared with the placebo group, which showed a 2.1% increase (95% CI –1.4–5.6%). Secondary outcomes included changes in lactate threshold and perceived exertion. The supplement was well tolerated, with no serious adverse events reported. These findings suggest that the supplement may enhance aerobic endurance in young adults, potentially through improved mitochondrial efficiency and glycogen sparing.
table_data:
Variable | Group A (Supplement) | Group B (Placebo)
--- | --- | ---
Baseline VO2max (ml/kg/min) | 45.2 ± 4.1 | 44.8 ± 3.9
TTE change from baseline (%) | 12.5 ± 16.6 | 2.1 ± 13.8
Lactate threshold (mmol/L) | 4.8 ± 0.6 | 4.5 ± 0.5
Perceived exertion (Borg) | 13.2 ± 1.1 | 13.5 ± 1.0
stem: Which of the following best describes the change in time to exhaustion (TTE) observed in the supplement group compared with the placebo group?
explanation: The supplement group’s mean TTE increased by 12.5% with a 95% confidence interval of 8.3–16.7%, whereas the placebo group’s increase was only 2.1% with a CI that includes zero.
trap: Pairing the supplement effect with the placebo group confidence interval (-1.4 to 5.6%).

stem: Which design feature allows the researchers to attribute the larger TTE gain in the supplement group to the supplement rather than to simply repeating the treadmill test?

options.A: A matched placebo group that took the same treadmill test
options.B: Baseline VO2max measured only in the supplement group
options.D: Measuring lactate threshold as a secondary outcome

explanation: Correct: The placebo group repeated the same test, so any practice effect appears in both groups and the extra gain in the supplement group (12.5% vs 2.1%) can be attributed to the supplement. Why the others are wrong: B) baseline VO2max is reported for both groups in the table. C) an age restriction affects generalizability, not practice effects. D) a secondary outcome does not separate practice effects from treatment effects.
trap: Choosing a study characteristic (age range or extra outcome) that does not involve a comparison group.

stem: Which statement about the secondary outcomes in the table is supported?

options.A: Mean lactate threshold was 0.3 mmol/L higher in the supplement group than in the placebo group.
options.B: Mean perceived exertion (Borg) was higher in the supplement group than in the placebo group.
options.C: Baseline VO2max differed between groups by more than 5 ml/kg/min.
options.D: Mean lactate threshold was lower in the supplement group than in the placebo group.

explanation: Correct: The table lists lactate threshold of 4.8 mmol/L (supplement) and 4.5 mmol/L (placebo), a difference of 0.3. Why the others are wrong: B) Borg values are 13.2 (supplement) and 13.5 (placebo), so exertion was lower, not higher. C) baseline VO2max was 45.2 and 44.8, a difference of 0.4. D) 4.8 is greater than 4.5.
trap: Assuming the supplement group must have had higher perceived exertion because it performed longer.
